claude_code.how: Apply the upstream generic LLM workflow through the available shell: encode selected JSON, provide the result in a toon code fence, and strictly decode generated TOON. No dedicated first-party Claude Code hook, plugin, MCP server or subagent installer was found in the checked release documentation; applying the CLI workflow to Claude is an adaptation.

codex.how: Use the same on-demand CLI/SDK encode-and-strict-decode workflow in a Codex task or worker. official_baseline_claims.claim: GitHub latest identifies latest_release v4.1.1, published 2026-08-05T11:49:55Z, establishing latest_date 2026-08-05; npm @toon-format/cli latest is also 4.1.1, published 2026-08-05T11:50:41.210Z (https://registry.npmjs.org/@toon-format%2Fcli).
The checked upstream retrieval benchmark reports TOON accuracy 72.2%, JSON accuracy 71.4%, and 42.6% fewer tokens. These are benchmark-specific results, not this repository's adapted performance.
Token-efficiency benchmarks use gpt-tokenizer/o200k_base and primarily compare against formatted JSON with two-space indentation; the documentation separately includes compact JSON comparisons.

Uniform arrays and keyed objects can share a tabular header; uniform nested object columns can also fold into nested field groups. Deeply nested or non-uniform structures may be less efficient than compact JSON.

limitations.text: The upstream nested e-commerce benchmark is +5.6% versus compact JSON, despite being smaller than formatted JSON. Source: docs/guide/benchmarks.md:300-315. Baseline formatting therefore materially changes a savings claim.

The specific rule 'only uniform arrays of 5 or more flat records' is UNVERIFIED as an upstream claim. No such minimum was found across the checked release's docs and package Markdown or encoder eligibility logic. extractTabularFields rejects an empty array, empty record fields and incompatible shapes, not arrays shorter than five. Correctness and positive token savings are separate questions.

There are other explicit counts that must not be confused with a five-record cutoff: keyed tabular objects require at least two entries, and the prompting guide recommends examples of 2–5 rows. Uniform nested columns are supported, so 'flat records only' is also narrower than upstream. Prompt-example source: https://github.com/toon-format/toon/blob/v4.1.1/docs/guide/llm-prompts.md#L179-L183

CLI --stats calls tokenx.estimateTokenCount on input JSON text and encoded TOON, not the benchmark's exact o200k_base tokenizer. It is a per-conversion estimate, not a cumulative provider-savings counter.

Open upstream issue #339 reports root strings beginning with U+FEFF being emitted unquoted and changing content or type on decode. PR #343 remains open, draft and unmerged in the live check; strict syntax validation alone is not proof of value preservation. Fix status: https://github.com/toon-format/toon/pull/343
The upstream ecosystem links Tooner as a separate MCP proxy. Installing the TOON CLI alone does not enable that transport integration.

native_adaptation.how_we_install: ~/code/native-agent-stack/manifests/stack.json pins TOON 4.1.1. adoption/pins-linux-x86_64.json and adoption/pins-macos-arm64.json identify the npm @toon-format/cli archive; adoption/bootstrap-linux.sh uses the versioned npm installation. recipes/README.md:113 gives npm install --global --prefix "$STACK_HOME/tools/toon-4.1.1" @toon-format/cli@4.1.1. This is the CLI package, not a dedicated MCP server.
native_adaptation.claude_wiring: On-demand Bash conversion: toon IN.json --stats -o OUT.toon, then toon OUT.toon --decode --strict -o BACK.json and compare decoded values (docs/token-session-handbook.md:137; recipes/README.md:113). adoption/templates/claude.settings.template.json has no TOON hook; none of the checked examples/claude-native/agents/*.md explicitly names TOON, so worker briefs need to supply the chosen representation and recovery requirement.
native_adaptation.codex_wiring: The CLI is available for explicit shell use and task-envelope data. Neither adoption/templates/codex.config.template.toml nor repo .codex/config.toml contains TOON-specific integration; those configurations do not provide automatic conversion. docs/token-session-handbook.md:137 explicitly lists TOON as on-demand structured-data conversion.
native_adaptation.lane_rule: Choose one useful context method per artifact; keep compact JSON when TOON expands it (docs/token-session-handbook.md:106-113,137). Require strict decoding plus semantic value comparison, including numeric precision (recipes/README.md:113). Treat --stats as an estimate and separate it from the evidence card's exact named-tokenizer comparisons.

final_verdict.summary: Installed TOON 4.1.1 is current and the selective CLI conversion with compact-JSON fallback matches upstream practice, but strict decoding alone does not guarantee value preservation (https://github.com/toon-format/toon/releases/tag/v4.1.1; https://github.com/toon-format/toon/blob/v4.1.1/packages/cli/README.md). The eligible 60-row uniform-table comparisons are 1642→907 o200k_base tokens (44.8%) in both Claude and Codex, whereas the nested catalog is 121472→132861 (+9.4%) and is ineligible as a saving, so compact JSON should be retained (../html-report/savings.json#report_comparisons). A separate two-row comparison saves 29→22 (24.1%), refuting an upstream five-row minimum, while a fresh installed-version check strictly decodes a BOM-prefixed string into a boolean (../rr/toon/out/12-stack-compare-o200k.sanitized.stdout; groups/verdict-evidence.json#toon_bom_check). The retained scan labels 62/1010 Ultracode workflow children (6.14%, 308 CLI matches), 3/301 eligible Codex workers (1.00%, 10 CLI matches), and 0/22 workflow_children_with_lanes_block as users; it does not count suitable conversion opportunities (invoke_by_tool.json). Next, replace the unqualified size heuristic with measured compact-JSON comparison and semantic round-trip checks, including the BOM case, before expanding use.
